Playbook.name: Endpoint — Security Agent (AV/EDR) Files Deleted or Replaced - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: AV/EDR agent files (Kaspersky/Defender/EDR install paths) were deleted or created/replaced (FIM). Triage: an attacker removing/replacing the security agent to disable protection, or a legitimate agent update/uninstall?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Deleting or replacing security-agent files disables endpoint protection - a direct defense-evasion step.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows FIM (verified; monitors Windows paths). Agent install paths for Kaspersky/Defender/EDR.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the agent-file change is malicious tampering or a legitimate update/uninstall.

Step.name: Agent files changed on the host
Step.Purpose: Which agent files were deleted/replaced and by what action reveals tampering vs update.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE event.dataset == "fim.event" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action IN ("deleted","created","updated") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | WHERE file.path RLIKE "(?i).*(kaspersky|windows defender|sense|sentinel|crowdstrike|endpoint).*" | KEEP @timestamp, event.action, file.path, file.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Deletion of agent binaries (not during an update) = tampering. Creation/replacement with modified binaries = agent replacement. An update replaces files under a version change window; a delete-without-reinstall is suspicious.

Step.name: Did the host show other tampering/suspicious activity
Step.Purpose: Agent-file deletion alongside other suspicious activity confirms defense evasion.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4688","1102","7045","4624") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Process execution, log-clear or service install around the agent-file change supports active tampering.

Node.Condition: Agent binaries deleted without a reinstall, or replaced with modified files, especially amid other suspicious activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Agent Tampering - IR, restore protection)

Node.Condition: A documented agent update/upgrade replacing files under a version window.
A sanctioned agent uninstall (decommission) under a change.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-AGENTFILE-CHANGE, INV-02-AGENTFILE-CONTEXT to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the update; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker removing/replacing the security agent.

SOCAction.Item: Restore the agent; isolate the host; open IR.
Reconstruct the unprotected window; hunt peers.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the affected endpoint (destination.domain) and the threat.
If malware active/uncured or spreading, isolate the endpoint.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Restore the agent; isolate the host; reconstruct the unprotected window.
Hunt the same tampering on peers.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure agent self-protection/tamper-protection is enabled; alert on agent-file changes.

QualityChecks.Check: Windows FIM monitors these paths; Linux agent paths are not covered (no Linux FIM).

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Agent restored; host contained; unprotected window reconstructed.
